about: Agents vs speed (build.py data.curves, src/model.js curve*, node report.js --curve, the page's Agents tab). Every ledger row that measured aggregate tok/s at two or more agent counts is a fit point set; rows with the same box, model, engine, build and engine flags pool into one config. Per config the batched decode law n / total = A x max(G, S) + B x max(G, S) x n / G (G = batch groups in use, S = pipeline stages) is fitted to the measured (n, total) pairs; A and B are the stage window's intercept and slope per agent, divided by 1000 x the pipeline efficiency. Every number here is {v, tag, src}.

min_each_tps.src: a setting (report.js --min, or the box on the page): the headline readout is the largest agent count with each agent at or above this many tok/s, and the total there

second_each_tps.src: a setting (report.js --second): the secondary readout, agents at or above this many tok/s each

agents_max.src: a setting (report.js --max): the curve runs from 1 agent to this many

min_points.src: two free constants (A, B) need two distinct agent counts; a config with fewer shows its points and no curve

table_n.src: the agent counts report.js --curve prints (the JSON carries every n); the readout counts are added

single_path_flags.src: XeStrata: with a drafter and batch MTP off, one agent runs the MTP single-stream path, not the batch window; its n = 1 point is kept out of the fit (shown, marked)

stage_window_re.src: the bench driver's layout_note form 'stage run n=32 45.87/45.03 ms': one ms per stage; the slowest stage is the window

power_field.src: measured.power_w in a ledger row: the watts that run measured, either one number for the run or {cN: W} per agent count like aggregate_tps; what it counts is the row's own measurement boundary, stated in the row (for example the cards' energy counters plus the CPU package, without the rest of the box), and is never assumed to be wall power

fit_warn_pct.src: a config whose fit misses a measured point by more than this many percent is flagged: the points do not follow the window law

slots.src: XeStrata --batch N: N agent slots; a point above N queued agents and is kept out of the fit

slots_each_point.src: the bench driver's sweep form '--batch=agents (one fresh server per agent count)': each point ran its own server with --batch n, so the host-pin check at n uses n slots

groups.src: XeStrata --batch-groups G (default 1): the agents split into G groups that take turns through the pipeline stages

split.src: the bench driver's engine_flags (older rows: conditions.isolation) 'layer split 25' (or '24,48'): one more stage than split points; none = one stage

kv.src: XeStrata --kv type (serving.kv); the flags, else conditions.kv_type

max_context.src: XeStrata --max-context or env MAX_CONTEXT (serving.max_context); else the recipe ctx
